summary: Small-fanout prefetch cascade leading to localized GPU thinning in eu-west reserved pool
description:
Issue summary: ClarifyAI (dedicated tenant) experienced sustained p99 and 429s for short streaming requests during midday window in eu-west. Root observable: a set of many small fanout streams (chatlets) with aggressive prefetch behavior caused a cascade of KV cache prefetch leases across multiple GPUs in the reserved pool, producing localized GPU thinness and slot fragmentation.

Impact: Customer observed elevated p50/p99 and intermittent 429s on their dedicated routes (~10-15% of requests in the 12:00-13:45 UTC window). Throughput to other tenants in the same reserved pool degraded modestly (3-7% p50 increase), and autoscaler failed to rapidly provision additional capacity due to a combination of cooldowns and fragmented slot availability.

Timeline (UTC):
- 11:57: first small fanout increase from ClarifyAI (many short streams, high keepalive)
- 12:05: kv-cache prefetch lease growth observed on pool-mgr logs
- 12:13: autoscaler sample shows elevated slot utilization but below scale-threshold due to fragmented free slots
- 12:22: support alert triggered by customer; 429s and p99 spikes visible in console
- 12:40: mitigation applied (temporary burst limit change and pinning)
- 13:05: partial recovery, p99 lowered but still above baseline

Observed metrics & logs: (excerpt)
[pool-mgr] 2026-03-13T12:06:11Z pool=eu-west-dedicated-5 lease_prefetch_count=124 slot_free=18 total_slots=256
[autoscaler] 2026-03-13T12:09:03Z pool=eu-west-dedicated-5 util=68.3% fragments=32 cooldown_remaining=420s decision=NO_SCALE
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-13T12:15:45Z route=/clarifyai/stream code=429 reason=slot_unavailable latency_p99=1120ms

Steps to reproduce (probabilistic):
1) Use a client that opens many short-lived streaming sessions (fanout 8-20 per conversation) with long keepalives and prefetch enabled.
2) Set model to gpt-medium-4o-q4 and run burst traffic at ~200rps for 10-30 minutes targeted at the dedicated pool.
3) Observe kv-cache lease growth across GPUs and increasing slot fragmentation; autoscaler increments do not trigger immediately because global util remains below the strict scaling threshold despite local fragmentation.

Initial hypothesis: aggressive prefetch logic combined with many short streams is allocating prefetch leases across GPUs leading to slot fragmentation. The autoscaler thresholds use aggregated utilization signals and a cooldown that prevents rapid response to fragmented availability. Noisy-neighbor behavior is not a single large tenant hogging GPU memory but many micro-streams scattering prefetch state and holding slots.

Immediate mitigation applied: increased ClarifyAI's allowed burst quota (to reduce failed requests while we investigate), temporarily pinned a small shard for their highest-throughput routes to limit pool-wide scatter, and raised autoscaler max-provision for pool eu-west-dedicated-5 from 4->6 to give headroom. These changes reduced 429 rate and lowered p99 by ~30%.

Recommended long-term fixes: tune prefetch lease lifetime and per-tenant prefetch limits, improve autoscaler signal to include fragmentation heuristics (free_contiguous_slots), and add a guard that converts many short streams into multiplexed connections to avoid slot-hogging.

References: Slack #support-eu thread https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SUPPORT/p1643_prefetch, infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8421 (autoscaler fragmentation metric), confluence runbook linked above.
investigation_notes:
Engineers pulled heap and lease metrics from pool-mgr, scheduler, and serving-runtime. Confirmed pattern: kv-cache prefetch lease_count correlates strongly (r=0.82) with slot fragmentation metric. Autoscaler logs show NO_SCALE decisions during the peak because global util stayed under threshold while free_contiguous_slots count fell below allocation limits. Checked GPU memory and drivers: no OOMs or kernel faults. No driver restarts in window. Hypothesis refined: prefetch leases are being spread across devices (fanout), preventing the allocator from finding contiguous slots to place new batches. Longer keepalives amplify the effect.

Action items from investigation:
- Collect sample of per-tenant lease distribution over next 48h (assigned to infra-monitoring).
- Prototype fragmentation-aware autoscaler rule (small PR drafted: see related_github_prs).
- Recommend customer apply client-side limiter (reduce fanout or enable multiplexing) as stopgap.

Notes: We saw similar mechanics in SUP-314159 but that incident was triggered by a different traffic mix; this ticket's distinguishing factor is many small concurrent streams with prefetch enabled and long keepalive, rather than one large noisy tenant.
comments: Aisha Khan (Support, 2026-03-13T12:25Z): Contacted ClarifyAI for traffic patterns and requested a sample client trace. Recommended temporary burst increase while we investigate.
ClarifyAI Ops (2026-03-13T12:30Z): Confirmed they rolled out a recent client change enabling eager prefetch in 2.1.0 of their SDK. They can toggle prefetch off for testing.
Marco Ruiz (SRE, 2026-03-13T12:38Z): Applied temporary shard pinning for route /clarifyai/high-prio and increased pool max nodes. Monitoring p99 and 429s now.
Nadia Patel (Infra, 2026-03-13T13:12Z): Drafted autoscaler augmentation PR to surface contiguous-slot metric; adding to pipeline for staging test.
resolution: Mitigations implemented: shard pinning + increased pool cap + customer burst uplift. Partial recovery achieved; p99 down ~30% from peak and 429s reduced to baseline-ish for most routes. Root cause: prefetch-cascade + slot fragmentation + autoscaler cooldown/aggregation semantics. Next steps: validate fragmentation-aware autoscaler in staging (infra), finalize client guidance to limit prefetch concurrency (support/solutions), and schedule a follow-up postmortem with ClarifyAI and infra team in 1 week. Owner for permanent fix: Marco Ruiz (SRE) and Nadia Patel (Infra).
